latest_nl_proof:
Let H_m := \sum_{j=1}^m \frac1j. Fix an integer n>1 and a real x with \frac{n-1}{n} \le x < 1.

For each k with 1 \le k \le n-1, we have
kx \ge k\cdot \frac{n-1}{n} = k - \frac{k}{n} > k-1,
because k<n implies \frac{k}{n}<1. Also kx<k since x<1. Hence k-1 < kx < k, so \lfloor kx\rfloor = k-1.
For k=n, we get n-1 \le nx < n, so \lfloor nx\rfloor = n-1.

Therefore
E(n,x)= (n-1)-\sum_{k=1}^{n-1}\frac{k-1}{k}-\frac{n-1}{n}.
Now \frac{k-1}{k}=1-\frac1k, so
\sum_{k=1}^{n-1}\frac{k-1}{k} = (n-1)-\sum_{k=1}^{n-1}\frac1k = (n-1)-H_{n-1}.
Substituting,
E(n,x)= (n-1)-\bigl((n-1)-H_{n-1}\bigr)-\frac{n-1}{n} = H_{n-1}-\frac{n-1}{n}.
Since H_n = H_{n-1}+\frac1n, this equals
H_n-1.
Thus E(n,x)=H_n-1 for every x in \left[\frac{n-1}{n},1\right).
role_in_parent: Exhibit a full family of maximizers and compute the common value on the top interval.
statement_nl: Let n be an integer greater than 1. If x is a real number with (n-1)/n <= x < 1, then E(n, x) = H_n - 1.

domain_restrictions: n is an integer and n > 1
x is a real number satisfying (n-1)/n <= x
x is a real number satisfying x < 1
the expressions (n-1)/n and H_n are assumed to be well-defined for the stated n
statement_semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: For every integer n greater than 1, and for every real number x with (n-1)/n <= x < 1, the value E(n, x) equals H_n minus 1.
quantifier_order: for all n in integers with n > 1
for all x in real numbers with (n-1)/n <= x and x < 1
